message.content:
Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) belong to two different orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively.  
Their most recent common ancestor is the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which includes Carnivora, Perissodactyla, Cetartiodactyla, Chiroptera, Pholidota, and a few other groups.  

This ancestor was a small placental mammal that lived roughly 90–100 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous, before the diversification of the modern orders that make up Laurasiatheria.
